Article Title: 'NC’s position no different from BJP': Srinagar MP accepts Farooq Abdullah's challenge, likely to resign
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Jammu and Kashmir National Conference's estranged MP from Srinagar Aga Ruhullah Mehdi on Friday said he will resign from Parliament, accusing party chief Farooq Abdullah and the NC leadership of abandoning the fight for restoration of Article 370 , despite securing a mandate on the issue in the 2024 Assembly elections.In a two-page letter to Abdullah, Mehdi sought answers over the party's change in its position on Article 370. His remarks came after Abdullah asked him to seek a fresh mandate for opposing the party line.Referring to Abdullah's recent statement urging Kashmiris to become self-reliant instead of seeking economic concessions from the Centre, Mehdi said the remarks reflected his own frustration with being expected to adopt a “posture of supplication” before the BJP.He questioned why the party leadership objected when he raised similar concerns over Jammu and Kashmir's constitutional rights.“The uncomfortable truth is that we are not even 'begging' for Article 370; we are 'begging' for statehood – a right the Supreme Court itself has recognised,” Mehdi said, arguing that the NC's current position had become indistinguishable from that of BJP.The letter came amid reports that Mehdi is likely to resign from the Lok Sabha on November 3, the death anniversary of his father Aga Syed Mehdi, who was assassinated in an IED blast on November 3, 2000.Mehdi warned that treating statehood as the limit of political aspirations could legitimise the constitutional changes made in August 2019 and weaken protections for Jammu and Kashmir's land, culture and environment.He also questioned NC's decision to move away from its 2024 assembly election promise of restoring Articles 370 and 35A.“Today, we conveniently argue that the very regime which abrogated Article 370 will never restore it… That would have been a fair argument. But the BJP was also in power when we drafted our 2024 manifesto. So, why did we include the restoration of Article 370 in our manifesto?” he asked.“Were we making promises we knew we could not keep or perhaps never truly intended to keep? Did we invoke the wound inflicted on the people of Jammu and Kashmir in August 2019 merely to derive political mileage, only to conveniently forget our promises after government formation?” he added.Pointing out that nearly 65 per cent of Jammu and Kashmir's population is young, Mehdi said their future was “increasingly uncertain” due to a lack of jobs and opportunities.“Our land is up for grabs. Our resources benefit everybody but us. Our religious rights, traditions, and language face constant pressure. Our environment is being ravaged by illegal deforestation, mining, and construction in ecologically fragile zones,” the Srinagar MP said.He said elected representatives must fight “this constant degradation and dehumanisation” instead of limiting public aspirations to what the BJP was willing to concede.“It is to ensure that the extraordinary and deeply consequential events of August 2019 do not become the new political normal and to recognise that restoration of statehood cannot be treated as an adequate substitute for what was taken away,” Mehdi said."Rest assured, the resignation will come. It would have come even without you asking, but before that must come accountability," he added.The letter comes at a time when reports suggest that the Srinagar MP is likely to resign from the Lok Sabha on November 3, coinciding with the death anniversary of his father Aga Syed Mehdi, who was assassinated by terrorists in an IED blast on November 3, 2000.
Article Summary: National Conference's estranged MP from Srinagar Aga Ruhullah Mehdi said he will resign from Parliament. He accused party chief Farooq Abdullah and the NC leadership of abandoning the fight for restoration of Article 370. His remarks came after Abdullah asked him to seek a fresh mandate for opposing the party line.

Article Title: UNCCD concludes COP17 with new drought resilience and land restoration initiatives
Article Text:
UNCCD conference in Mongolia set the stage for enhanced global drought resilience with innovative initiatives.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The seventeenth session of the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD) conference concluded in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia, on Friday by presenting a new global architecture for drought resilience that will help countries bridge the gap between plans and implementation.Multiple new initiatives were announced during the 12-day conference (COP17). They include $1.3 billion in new and pipeline finance for land restoration and strengthening drought resilience in vulnerable countries.These initiatives — the world’s first Drought Resilience Index (DRI) and the Drought Resilience Investment Facility (DRIF) — will help countries in assessing their capacity to anticipate, prepare for and adapt to drought, and unlock much larger flows of institutional and private finance for projects that strengthen water security, sustainable agriculture, nature-based solutions and land restoration.DRI’s technical monitoring metrics will enable countries to identify vulnerabilities and inform more effective policies and investments. Its new AI-powered features can help policymakers, technical experts and the public interpret complex data and turn it into practical insights.DRIF, on the other hand, aims to mobilise up to $400 million in public and private capital for drought resilience. The facility, launched by UNCCD and Luxembourg, will use public capital to reduce investment risks.“We came to Ulaanbaatar saying that COP17 must be a COP of implementation. We leave with more of the architecture needed to make that possible: political decisions, stronger science, innovative financing mechanisms, investment pipelines and partnerships that can move solutions to scale,” said UNCCD executive secretary Yasmine Fouad.The conference took place against a stark global backdrop as up to 40 percent of the world’s land is degraded, while countries have committed to restoring more than one billion hectares, including 26 million hectares by India, by 2030. India was represented by a team led by Union environment minister Bhupender Yadav at COP17.
Article Summary: Multiple new initiatives were announced during the 12-day conference (COP17) They include $1.3 billion in new and pipeline finance for land restoration and strengthening drought resilience in vulnerable countries. India was represented by a team led by Union environment minister Bhupender Yadav at COP17.

NEW DELHI: Bharatiya Janata Party 's Punjab unit disciplinary committee on Friday issued show-cause notices to three of its leaders for making statements about party's internal affairs and organisational matters.The notices have been issued to former Sangrur district presidents Randeep Singh Deol, Maninder Singh Kapial and Jatinder Kalra.The disciplinary committee said that such conduct prima facie adversely affected the party's reputation, credibility and organisational image.The party has directed the individuals to submit their written explanations within 7 days of receiving the notice, explaining why disciplinary action should not be initiated against them for allegedly violating party discipline and damaging the party's reputation.The notices further seek specific clarification regarding each individual's role in the press conference, statements made by them, and the purpose of the press conference.This comes after the three leaders held a press conference in Sangrur on August 25.Recent organisational reshuffle in BJP led to dissent among sections of leaders who accused the state leadership of sidelining the old cadre.This comes after BJP's state in charge BL Santosh began his two-day visit to Punjab to review the party's organisational functioning and strengthen coordination and preparedness at the grassroots level in the poll-bound state.

Article Title: Uttarakhand CM Dhami announces free bus travel, Pink e-Buses for women on Raksha Bandhan
Article Text:
Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami revealed a series of initiatives aimed at empowering women

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami on Raksha Bandhan announced a series of measures aimed at improving women’s safety, mobility and economic empowerment, including free travel in Roadways buses for women aged 60 years and above.The announcements were made during a Raksha Bandhan programme at Chakarpur Stadium, where women tied rakhis to Dhami. The chief minister said the initiatives reflected the government’s commitment to women’s dignity, safety and self-reliance.Under the new provision, women aged 60 years and above will be able to travel free of cost in Roadways buses. The facility was earlier available to senior citizens above 65 years of age.Dhami also announced that 10 of the 100 electric buses to be operated in Dehradun under the PM e-Bus Sewa will be dedicated to women as Pink e-Buses. He said the facility would subsequently be expanded to other parts of Uttarakhand in phases to provide women with safer and more convenient public transport.The government has also increased the concessional bank loan limit under the Women’s Self-Employment Scheme from Rs 2 lakh to Rs 2.50 lakh.Dhami said the move was intended to provide women with greater access to capital and encourage them to become employment providers rather than only job seekers.He further announced plans to develop modern, high-tech toilets with contemporary facilities at major public places, markets, tourist destinations and other important locations across the state. The facilities will focus on cleanliness, privacy, safety and convenience for women.Addressing the gathering, Dhami said women’s dignity and safety were among the government’s highest priorities. He said Raksha Bandhan was not only a celebration of the bond between brothers and sisters but also a reminder of responsibility, respect and commitment towards women.Dhami highlighted schemes including the Nanda Gaura Yojana, Chief Minister Mahalakshmi Kit Yojana, 181 Women Helpline and One Stop Centres. He also said women have been provided 30 percent horizontal reservation in government services.The chief minister said 3.09 lakh women in Uttarakhand had become Lakhpati Didis. He urged them to set a bigger goal of becoming Crorepati Didis and assured them of continued government support.He also highlighted interest-free loans of up to Rs 5 lakh for Self-Help Groups and the Mukhyamantri Sashakt Bahna Utsav Yojana, under which women are being provided better market access for their products.
Article Summary: Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami announced a series of measures aimed at improving women’s safety, mobility and economic empowerment. The announcements were made during a Raksha Bandhan programme at Chakarpur Stadium, where women tied rakhis to the chief minister.
